title: Iterative Latent Refinement for Value Learning in Offline Goal-Conditioned RL
summary: Replacing static single-pass value networks with weight-reusing iterative latent dynamics improves long-horizon value estimation and policy extraction across offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning benchmarks without altering training objectives or feedforward actors.
question: Can weight-reusing iterative latent dynamics outperform static feedforward networks when learning long-horizon value and compatibility functions?
motivation: Standard deep learning backbones map inputs to predictions in a single feedforward pass, allocating fixed computation regardless of structural difficulty. From an architecture-dynamics-function perspective, weight-reusing recurrent updates turn a static network into a discrete-time dynamical system that iteratively refines internal representations. Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning provides a stringent testbed for this principle: from fixed trajectories alone, a critic or value network must stitch multi-step routes across bottlenecks while providing a stable action-scoring interface.
idea: We replace only the feedforward multilayer perceptron inside the value, critic, or compatibility network of Contrastive RL (CRL), HIQL, and SAW while holding datasets, losses, and feedforward actors unchanged. An input-conditioned latent state evolves over \(K\) outer refinement steps that reuse \(m\) inner update blocks. Each inner block combines pre-LayerNorm, step embeddings, and input-dependent SwiGLU gating, while outer LayerScale coefficients initialize residual state updates at small magnitude so repeated weight application refines the trajectory stably before linear readout.
finding_title: Controlled Dynamical Compute Allocation
finding: Across 21 OGBench locomotion and manipulation comparisons, four-step refinement raises mean success by 10.5 percentage points, including jumps from 53% to 95% on medium-stitch and 11% to 48% on large-stitch AntMaze in CRL. Parameter-matched wider (53%) and deeper (48%) feedforward critics fail to close this gap, and recurrent refinement retains clear gains at matched training FLOPs (86% versus 51% on medium-stitch). Diagnostics show stronger normalized goal separation and actor actions closer to dataset support, while ablations confirm that moderate depth, task-matched per-step capacity, LayerNorm, and LayerScale are essential to prevent over-refinement.
diagram_caption: Overview of iterative latent refinement for offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning.
version_note: Daoxin Li and Songcheng Xu contributed equally.

title: A Kernel-Spectral Index for Single-Neuron Input-Output Complexity
summary: The Spectral Complexity Index quantifies single-neuron input-output nonlinearity by counting the kernel eigenmodes needed to capture somatic responses, linking dendritic and synaptic biophysics to representational dimensionality at one-tenth the cost of deep network surrogates.
question: How many orthogonal input-history modes are required to capture the nonlinear input-output computation of a biophysical cortical neuron?
motivation: Unlike point units in standard artificial neural networks, biological neurons transform distributed synaptic inputs through steep biophysical nonlinearities, including dendritic filtering, active sodium and calcium conductances, and voltage-dependent NMDA currents. While these nonlinear dynamics expand single-cell expressive capacity, they also make brain-inspired networks difficult to analyze and train. Existing benchmarks quantify single-neuron complexity by fitting multi-layer temporal convolutional surrogates, leaving the underlying input-output geometry opaque and requiring thousands of simulations per cell.
idea: We formulate the Spectral Complexity Index (SCI) on raw presynaptic spike histories organized across 200 channels spanning excitatory and inhibitory types, basal and apical dendritic domains, and normalized electrotonic distance. A time-decayed Gaussian kernel defines an explicit similarity geometry that resolves recent events finely and older events coarsely. Projecting the centered somatic voltage response onto the ordered Mercer eigenfunctions of this kernel operator, SCI counts the minimum number of leading linear spectral modes required to explain 80% of somatic response energy.
finding_title: Cross-Species Separation and NMDA Sensitivity
finding: Evaluated on 35 biophysically detailed human and mouse cortical neuron models calibrated to matched firing rates, SCI reveals that human pyramidal and aspiny neurons require significantly deeper spectral expansions than mouse neurons, indicating richer high-frequency spatiotemporal sensitivity. SCI rankings correlate strongly with deep-network Functional Complexity Index scores across all cells (Spearman \(\rho = 0.797\)) while reducing required simulations from 12,000 to between 100 and 1,000 ten-second traces and cutting total compute cost at least tenfold. Silencing NMDA receptors in spiny human models significantly lowers SCI, directly linking active synaptic nonlinearity to higher representational dimensionality.
diagram_caption: Kernel-spectral decomposition of presynaptic histories quantifies how many modes drive somatic output energy.

title: Softmax Attention with Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching the Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds
summary: Exploiting low-dimensional query-key geometry and exponential score decay yields subquadratic softmax attention algorithms across arbitrary positive temperatures, matching the best known batch maximum-inner-product complexity bounds in every fixed dimension.
question: How do spatial dimension and temperature-controlled exponential weighting govern the fundamental time complexity of global softmax attention?
motivation: Softmax attention connects geometric representation structure to global context integration by converting query-key inner products into a Boltzmann-weighted average across tokens, with temperature tuning the regime from diffuse averaging to sharp selection. Direct evaluation computes all quadratic pairwise interactions even when queries and keys lie in fixed or low-rank dimensions. A central theoretical question is whether aggregating all exponentially weighted tokens is inherently harder than finding only the single strongest maximum-inner-product match.
idea: Subtracting row maxima isolates near-maximal keys within a logarithmic score window while bounding discarded exponential tails within target additive error. In two dimensions, centering the key hull and sweeping radial-boundary polynomial moments solves attention deterministically in near-linear time. In higher fixed dimensions, Lagrange temperature interpolation decouples query norms, and shallow-cutting ray shooting with random doubling prefixes and heavy-light recursion partitions active pairs into disjoint common-anchor blocks that reduce inductively to lower-dimensional shifted-kernel products.
finding_title: Matching Best Known Inner-Product Exponents
finding: For \(m\) queries and \(n\) keys in fixed dimension \(d\), expected runtime scales as \(\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\bigl((mn)^{k/(k+1)} + m + n\bigr)\) with \(k = \lfloor d/2 \rfloor\) and polylogarithmic dependence on coordinate bounds and inverse error, supporting any positive temperature. For \(m = n\), this improves the prior \(n^{2-1/d}\) bound to near-linear time in dimensions two and three and \(n^{4/3}\) in dimensions four and five, matching the best known batch maximum-inner-product bound in every fixed dimension. Conversely, exact integer batch maximum inner product reduces to one attention call in the same dimension.
diagram_caption: Geometric query-key structure in fixed dimension enables subquadratic attention across arbitrary positive temperatures.

title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation
summary: Motivated by emergent power-law spatial correlations in trained diffusion models, Scale-Free Attention embeds a parameter-free multiscale hierarchy that reduces attention to \(\mathcal{O}(N\log N)\) complexity, accelerating high-resolution generation while outperforming full attention on ImageNet.
question: Can embedding natural scale-free spatial correlation priors into attention topology accelerate iterative diffusion generation while improving visual quality?
motivation: High-resolution diffusion and flow-matching transformers generate images through iterative denoising dynamics, but all-to-all self-attention imposes a quadratic token bottleneck at every step. Examining pretrained PixelFlow-XL reveals a clear link between natural image physics and learned interaction dynamics: whereas random initialization produces flat spatial attention, trained radial attention decays with distance as a power law (exponent 1.414, \(R^2 = 0.974\)), mirroring scale-free correlations in statistical physics and motivating a multiscale interaction architecture.
idea: Scale-Free Attention (SFA) preserves exact token interactions within a local neighborhood (up to 144 tokens) while partitioning distant regions through a shared quadtree into progressively coarser mean-pooled blocks (at most 27 blocks per scale, totaling \(\mathcal{O}(\log N)\) representatives per query). Adding the logarithm of each block's token count to its mean logit under one shared softmax across all scales introduces zero extra parameters, uniquely minimizes reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence among blockwise uniform distributions, and acts as a variance-reducing far-field filter.
finding_title: Multi-Hundred-Fold Kernel Speedups and Stronger FID
finding: Fused Triton kernels achieve \(\mathcal{O}(N\log N)\) forward and backward passes, reaching \(357.3\times\) forward and \(265.6\times\) backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens and \(25.75\times\) faster end-to-end training on \(512 \times 512\) FFHQ. Trained from scratch on ImageNet \(256 \times 256\), PixelFlow with SFA improves 40-epoch FID-50k from 13.25 for full attention to 12.51 (raising Inception Score from 94.23 to 101.20), an advantage maintained through 80 epochs. Replacing full attention in pretrained PixelFlow and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium preserves generation quality under matched fine-tuning budgets.
diagram_caption: Fine local interactions combine with progressively pooled distant regions under one shared attention distribution.

title: Connectome-to-Function: Conditional Generative Latent Representations for Reservoir Computing
summary: An unsupervised conditional generative model compresses single-cell cortical connectomes into a continuous structural latent space whose coordinates predict reservoir computing performance and reveal distinct wiring mechanisms for memory, forecasting, and classification.
question: Can a compact generative representation learned solely from biological connectomes explain how synaptic circuit structure shapes dynamical computation?
motivation: Single-cell connectomes map thousands of synaptic connections alongside three-dimensional soma positions and excitatory or inhibitory cell identities, offering a direct empirical window into how neural architecture governs dynamics and function. Yet connectome graphs are sparse and high-dimensional: predefined graph statistics cannot synthesize new circuits, while task-trained predictors entangle structural representation with a single objective. Bridging connectomics and computation requires an unsupervised generative space that preserves multi-node topology and exposes functional axes.
idea_title: Spatial-Conditional Connectome VAE and Reservoir Probing
idea: Using 498 laminar microcircuit columns extracted from the mouse MICrONS connectome, we train a permutation-invariant conditional variational autoencoder combining PointNet++ spatial embeddings, graph attention, and Transformer encoders and decoders conditioned on soma coordinates and cell types without task supervision. Decoding latent vectors under shared node templates generates Dale-signed recurrent matrices normalized to a fixed spectral radius, isolating how topological variation shapes recurrent reservoir dynamics across copy memory, chaotic Lorenz forecasting, and sequential MNIST classification.
finding_title: Predictable Function and Task-Specific Wiring Mediators
finding: Across held-out mouse cortical columns, the conditional generative model reconstructs synaptic connectivity with 0.910 edge AUC while compressing circuit topology into a continuous latent space whose coordinates predict reservoir performance on delayed memory copy, chaotic Lorenz forecasting, and sequential MNIST classification (\(R^2\) up to 0.65, 0.46, and 0.87). Observational mediation analysis further identifies task-specific candidate partial mediators linking circuit structure, dynamical properties, and function within the same latent space: mixed excitatory-inhibitory reciprocity is associated with delayed memory retention, lower non-normality is associated with reduced transient amplification in chaotic forecasting, and higher stable rank is associated with sequential classification performance.
diagram_caption: Connectome graphs map into a conditional latent space that links wiring motifs to function.

title: Global Credit Assignment via Dynamical Criticality
summary: By placing recurrent and spiking networks in a stable near-critical dynamical regime, Criticality-driven Online Local Alignment uses emergent spatiotemporal correlations to approximate global credit assignment in constant activation memory and \(\mathcal{O}(H)\) state.
question: Can the long-range spatiotemporal correlations of near-critical neural dynamics turn strictly local online updates into accurate global credit assignment?
motivation: Nonlinear cellular and recurrent dynamics give biological and neuromorphic networks rich temporal capacity, yet training them over long horizons faces a severe credit-assignment bottleneck. Backpropagation through time stores full state trajectories in \(\mathcal{O}(TH)\) activation memory and propagates gradients through long nonlinear Jacobian chains prone to vanishing or exploding, while existing online approximations still require synapse-scale \(\mathcal{O}(H^2)\) auxiliary states or incur heavy bias. Cortical circuits operating near criticality naturally exhibit persistent temporal echoes and spatial coherence that can carry credit signals forward.
idea_title: Near-Critical Scalar Closure of Error Recursion
idea: COLA initializes recurrent weights in a stable near-critical band (maximum Lyapunov exponent just below zero) using a lightweight operator-normalized two-point Lyapunov probe. Within this regime, temporal persistence and spatial mode alignment across units allow the reverse-time gradient recursion to close algebraically within each time step. Tracking only two exponential-moving-average scalars per hidden unit, a temporal continuation factor and an effective recurrent loop gain, yields a closed-form online update requiring \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) activation memory and \(\mathcal{O}(H)\) auxiliary state.
finding_title: Long-Horizon Stability Across RNNs and Spiking Networks
finding: COLA excels where long backward Jacobian chains destabilize training, reducing Adding-problem MSE from 0.1426 (BPTT) to 0.0059 and chaotic Lorenz rollout MSE from 0.6841 (BPTT) and 0.1395 (UORO) to 0.0058, while outperforming full BPTT on character-level language modeling and remaining competitive with \(\mathcal{O}(H^2)\) online rules on row-sequential classification where multi-step BPTT remains strongest. Crucially, the rule transfers directly to nonlinear recurrent spiking networks (RLIF, RadLIF, and EGRU), matching or exceeding BPTT and pp-prop on four of five neuromorphic audio and vision pairings.
diagram_caption: Critical spatiotemporal correlations carry credit signals across time to guide local online updates.

title: The Hippocampal Place Field Gradient: A Bio-inspired Framework Building Multiscale Representation for Better Sample Efficiency
summary: Deriving how frequency-dependent decay of entorhinal grid projections generates the continuous dorsal-ventral hippocampal place field gradient reveals a spectral precision-generalization trade-off and inspires a multiscale Transformer positional embedding for data-efficient learning.
question: How do discrete grid-cell modules generate continuous multiscale place fields, and how does that structural gradient improve sample efficiency?
motivation: Along the dorsal-ventral axis of the hippocampus, place field widths expand continuously from fine local tuning to broad spatial integration, even though upstream medial entorhinal grid cells fire at discrete spatial scales. Resolving how circuit wiring transforms discrete periodic bases into a smooth multiscale population code, and why biological memory maintains redundant spatial resolutions rather than a single high-precision scale, links anatomical projection structure directly to inductive bias and few-shot generalization.
idea_title: Frequency-Decayed Grid Projections and Multiscale HIPE
idea: We analytically prove that Gaussian place fields of width \(\sigma_p\) emerge from periodic grid modules when projection weights decay exponentially with squared spatial frequency, predicting asymmetric dorsoventral connectivity. Kernel generalization theory over the induced population covariance spectrum then quantifies code-task alignment across sample sizes. Translating periodic grid phases to rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), we introduce Hippocampus-Inspired Positional Embedding (HIPE), applying Jacobian-compensated Gaussian frequency attenuation in deeper Transformer layers while preserving sharp RoPE in shallow layers without materializing dense bias matrices.
finding_title: Adaptive Few-Shot Generalization in Brains and Transformers
finding: Exponential frequency decay along dorsoventral grid-to-place projections reproduces the continuous biological place-field gradient without discrete modular boundaries. In spatial function learning, optimal single-scale place-field width tracks the target environment's characteristic spatial scale, and while a finely tuned single-scale model can reach peak performance on a specific task, a multiscale population performs consistently well across diverse environments and achieves higher average accuracy than any single-scale counterpart. Embedded into Transformers via a FlashAttention-compatible bipartite formulation (HIPE), this multiscale spatial inductive bias improves sample efficiency and sequence-length generalization.
diagram_caption: Frequency-dependent grid projections form multiscale spatial codes that guide data-efficient positional embeddings.
version_note: The linked earlier preprint has a different title and author list from the ICML conference version.

title: Aligning Inductive Bias for Data-Efficient Generalization in State Space Models
summary: Formalizing linear state space models as recurrent dynamical filters whose frequency response governs kernel mode learnability motivates Task-Dependent Initialization, aligning initial model spectra with task structure to accelerate finite-sample generalization.
question: How does the recurrent state dynamics of a linear state space model shape its spectral inductive bias for small-sample generalization?
motivation: A defining strength of brain-like computation is data-efficient generalization driven by structural and dynamical inductive biases rather than brute-force data scaling. Linear time-invariant state space models (SSMs) operate as continuous-time linear recurrent networks that both power modern long-sequence AI and parallel dynamical models of neural population filtering. However, standard SSMs rely on fixed, task-agnostic spectral initializations; when task-relevant frequencies fall into low-response bands of the recurrent filter, scarce training samples are spent overcoming an unfavorable prior.
idea_title: SSM-Induced Kernel Spectrum and Task-Dependent Initialization
idea: Viewing linear time-invariant State Space Models as continuous-to-discrete linear recurrent neural networks that abstract recurrent neural integration, we analyze finite-sample sequence learning through the causal Toeplitz convolution operator \(T_h\). For inputs of length \(L\) with general covariance \(\Sigma\), generalization dynamics depend on the effective operator \(T_h \Sigma^{1/2}\); under isotropic inputs (\(\mathbb{E}_u[uu^{\top}] = I_L\)) and the length-scaled singular value decomposition \(T_h = \sqrt{L}\, U S V^{\top}\), we prove that the inducing kernel eigenvalues equal the squared scaled singular values (\(\eta_{\rho} = s_{\rho}^{2}\)) and are asymptotically governed by the squared magnitude of the SSM frequency response. Based on this link, Task-Dependent Initialization aligns the initial recurrent spectrum with empirical target power spectra.
finding_title: Finite-Sample Gains Under Spectral Mismatch
finding: Kernel regression confirms that TDI shifts target power into leading kernel eigenmodes to reduce finite-sample error specifically when default low-frequency priors mismatch high-frequency tasks. In trainable one-layer SSMs, TDI improves low-data accuracy across all seven sequence benchmarks, including gains of 17.3 percentage points on sequential MNIST and 9.9 percentage points on ECG5000. Applied to the first layer of deep S4D models, TDI accelerates early learning (cutting epochs to 80% sequential MNIST accuracy at 2.15% data from 34.2 to 20.0) and boosts low-data performance on spectrally structured tasks, while baselines catch up given abundant data, extended training, or non-spectral compositional labels.
diagram_caption: Matching the state space kernel spectrum to task frequencies accelerates downstream generalization.

title: SpikeStereoNet: A Brain-Inspired Framework for Stereo Depth Estimation from Spike Streams
summary: SpikeStereoNet estimates dense stereo depth directly from microsecond spike camera streams through weight-reusing recurrent spiking refinement with provable dynamical stability and strong data efficiency.
question: How can binocular microsecond spike streams be transformed directly into accurate, data-efficient stereo depth?
motivation: Frame-based stereo cameras suffer motion blur and latency in fast scenes, whereas differential event cameras lose static surface texture. Retina-inspired spike cameras preserve both microsecond timing and continuous luminance through asynchronous photon accumulation, yet converting raw spikes back into synthetic frames reintroduces quantization blur and discards the temporal structure needed for sample-efficient 3D perception.
idea: SpikeStereoNet couples multiscale binocular spike feature and context extractors with a four-level correlation pyramid and a three-layer recurrent spiking neural network update operator. Across iterative weight-reusing steps, adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire neurons dynamically gate membrane retention, firing thresholds, and soft resets using contextual embeddings, while intra-layer recurrent and inter-layer feedforward convolutions propagate spatiotemporal disparity cues under firing-rate and voltage regularization.
finding_title: Contractive Refinement and Real-World Depth Accuracy
finding: Dynamical analysis confirms that hidden-state updates contract monotonically with final-step Jacobian eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle while principal-component trajectories separate diverse inputs. On a 190-scene synthetic benchmark, SpikeStereoNet reaches 0.42 px average error (4.13% bad-2.0) with 12.15M parameters and 473B FLOPs, outperforming larger frame and event baselines, and achieves 0.56 px error on a 3,000-pair 20,000 Hz real-world stereo spike dataset with widening gains at 10% to 50% training data.
diagram_caption: Binocular microsecond spike streams fuse through recurrent spiking updates to produce dense depth.

title: Redefining spiking neural networks through the lens of dynamical superspace
summary: This perspective introduces dynamical superspace, a theoretical taxonomy linking neuronal biophysics and connectome priors to non-equilibrium state dynamics and native neuromorphic functions.
question: What theoretical framework unites clock-driven deep learning with asynchronous, non-equilibrium biological computation?
motivation: Most modern spiking neural networks mimic synchronous artificial networks by quantizing rate activations on discrete global clocks. Treating spikes merely as low-bit activations obscures how biological architectures use continuous physical time, cellular heterogeneity, and non-equilibrium transient dynamics as computational resources, leaving spiking models benchmarked on static tasks mismatched to their physics.
idea: This review organizes neural architectures along two continuous axes, temporal information density and state-space complexity, spanning synchronous rate-coded networks (Level 0), clock-driven surrogate-gradient spiking networks (Level 1), event-driven spike-timing networks (Level 2), and biological non-equilibrium dynamics featuring multi-timescale adaptation, waves, attractors, and criticality (Level 3). It synthesizes how smooth spike topologies, local multiphasic plasticity, and innate connectome priors bridge optimization and physical execution.
finding_title: Roadmap for Native Temporal Intelligence
finding: Rather than forcing spiking systems to imitate static classifiers, the perspective identifies native regimes where Level 2 and Level 3 dynamics confer clear architectural advantages: microsecond always-on neuromorphic vision, low-latency closed-loop robotic control, ultra-low-power bio-signal interfaces, mesoscale cortical hypothesis testing, and recurrent infinite-horizon state compression complementing finite-window attention models.
diagram_caption: Neural computation ascends from synchronous rate codes to asynchronous, non-equilibrium dynamical trajectories.

title: Discovering heterogeneous synaptic plasticity rules via large-scale neural evolution
summary: Multi-objective evolution in a data-driven mouse V1 microcircuit discovers cell-type-specific local synaptic plasticity rules exhibiting computational degeneracy, cross-scale transfer, and rapid few-shot adaptation.
question: How do diverse cell-type-specific local synaptic plasticity rules coordinate within cortical circuits to drive adaptive visual function?
motivation: Neocortical synapses express diverse plasticity mechanisms across excitatory and inhibitory cell classes rather than a single uniform update rule, while global backpropagation through time remains biologically implausible and memory-intensive in realistic spiking circuits. Understanding how heterogeneous local rules jointly shape stable network dynamics and task learning requires searching high-dimensional rule spaces under physiological constraints.
idea: Within an anatomically constrained 3,000-neuron mouse primary visual cortex column spanning 17 excitatory and Pvalb, Sst, and Htr3a inhibitory cell classes, we parameterize 289 cell-type-pair-specific local plasticity rules via truncated Taylor expansions of pre- and postsynaptic spikes, eligibility traces, and global neuromodulatory error signals (2,645 total parameters), co-optimizing task accuracy alongside firing-rate and membrane-voltage regularizers via multi-objective evolutionary search without backpropagation.
finding_title: Degenerate Rule Families and Few-Shot Transfer
finding: Evolved heterogeneous plasticity ensembles outperform homogeneous local rules on orientation discrimination and visual change detection, transfer without re-evolution from 3,000-neuron training columns across V1 circuit scales spanning 1,000 to 5,000 neurons and unseen stimulus orientations, and enable rapid online adaptation to new visual tasks within the first 100 trials. Across independent runs, mathematically distinct excitatory-inhibitory rule motifs sustain sparse laminar dynamics and comparable accuracy, demonstrating computational degeneracy in cortical learning.
diagram_caption: Evolution searches high-dimensional synaptic rule spaces inside V1 to yield adaptable learning mechanisms.

title: Representation Transfer via Invariant Input-driven Continuous Attractors for Fast Domain Adaptation
summary: Task-agnostic synthetic pretraining sculpts modular recurrent networks into invariant input-driven continuous attractors that enable noise-resilient, parameter-efficient few-shot domain adaptation.
question: How can recurrent neural architectures form reusable dynamical manifolds that adapt rapidly across noisy sensory domains?
motivation: Monolithic video networks learn dataset-specific correlations that degrade under frame loss or viewpoint shifts, whereas random reservoirs lack structured inductive biases for complex spatiotemporal vision. Cortical motion pathways instead decompose sensory streams through modular circuits whose low-dimensional attractor geometries remain invariant across changing environments.
idea: Our Pretrained Reservoir Group (\(\sim 5\,\mathrm{M}\) parameters) pairs spatial encoders with three sparse excitatory-inhibitory layer-normalized recurrent modules pretrained exclusively on synthetic motion primitives, sculpting ring, toroidal, and cylindrical input-driven continuous attractors for direction, multiscale salience, and velocity. Without retraining recurrent weights, downstream domains fuse frozen module trajectories via unsupervised Hebbian correlation weighting and a lightweight readout adapter.
finding_title: Cross-Modal Transfer and Few-Shot Resilience
finding: These input-anchored manifolds track rapid transitions while recovering smoothly from up to 50% frame dropout. Transferred directly to 10-class event-based DVS Gesture (94% accuracy) and 15-class RGB Rehabilitation monitoring (89% to 90% macro-class accuracy), the 5M-parameter system achieves accuracy competitive with or exceeding 240M to 300M-parameter ResNet-C3D and ViViT models in minutes of adapter training, with pronounced gains in 5-shot learning (\(\sim 70\%\) on DVS and \(\sim 75\%\) macro accuracy on RGB).
diagram_caption: Task-agnostic recurrent modules form invariant attractor manifolds that adapt rapidly via lightweight adapters.

title: Decoding Cortical Microcircuits: A Generative Model for Latent Space Exploration and Controlled Synthesis
venue: NeuroAI Multimodal Intelligence Workshop at AAAI 2026
summary: A graph-attention and rotary-Transformer variational autoencoder compresses mouse visual cortex microcircuits into a continuous latent blueprint that links connectome motifs to reservoir computation and steers synthetic circuit generation.
question: Can high-dimensional cortical connectomes be compressed into a low-dimensional latent code that predicts dynamical function and guides circuit synthesis?
motivation: Electron-microscopy connectomes map thousands of synapses per cortical column, yet developmental biology builds these circuits from compact genetic rules rather than synapse-by-synapse lookup tables. Extracting a continuous low-dimensional representation of empirical microcircuits is essential for linking anatomical motifs to recurrent dynamics and synthesizing bio-plausible network architectures.
idea: From the mouse MICrONS visual cortex connectome, we extract 3,285 laminar columns of 80 to 100 depth-ordered neurons and encode their directed synaptic graphs into a 32-dimensional variational latent space using Graph Attention layers paired with Rotary Position Embedding Transformers. Linear topological gradients in latent space are combined with Metropolis-Hastings Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling for motif-constrained synthesis and reservoir evaluation.
finding_title: Controllable Synthesis and Reservoir Advantage
finding: The generative model accurately reproduces held-out cortical microcircuit degree, clustering, and motif distributions under Maximum Mean Discrepancy, Earth Mover's Distance, and Total Variation evaluations, organizes reciprocity, clustering, modularity, and degree dispersion along smooth latent axes, and synthesizes novel circuits matching target motif profiles. Evaluated as recurrent reservoirs, VAE-generated microcircuits lower memory-copy test loss by 51% to 58% relative to density-matched random reservoirs and trace monotonic accuracy trends on sequential MNIST across latent topological percentiles.
diagram_caption: Detailed microcircuit maps compress into a latent blueprint for functional analysis and synthesis.

title: Sparse cortical dynamics reveal flexible condition-dependent spike-order codes
summary: Comparing mouse V1 recordings with factorial ablations of a data-driven cortical microcircuit model shows that cellular diversity and local wiring turn sparse firing into flexible, condition-dependent spike-order codes.
question: What architectural constraints prevent sparse cortical activity from collapsing into rigid sequential firing pipelines?
motivation: Neocortical circuits compute with remarkably few spikes, concentrating neuronal responses into brief temporal windows despite strong trial-to-trial variability. Yet sparseness alone can produce stereotyped synfire-like chains; understanding how sparse cortical populations dynamically reorder spike timing across stimulus and task conditions requires isolating the structural origins of temporal flexibility.
idea_title: Factorial Dissection of Sparse Spike-Order Coding
idea: We analyze single-trial peak-latency rank orders across task conditions in mouse V1 Neuropixels recordings alongside a trained 51,978-neuron data-based V1 microcircuit model read out through layer-5 projection neurons. A balanced \(2 \times 2\) structural ablation independently removes 111-type GLIF3 neuronal diversity and laminar distance-dependent connectivity, complemented by activity-regularized rate-RNN baselines and targeted silencing of early informative neurons.
finding_title: Separable Structural Origins of Temporal Routing
finding: Spiking thresholds and metabolic regularization establish high dimensionless lifetime and population sparseness indices across all spiking variants by concentrating neuronal firing into brief temporal windows, yet generic recurrent spiking networks settle into comparatively rigid sequences with low condition-dependent rank-order divergence (\(D = 1 - \rho_{\mathrm{Spearman}}\)). Across stimulus and task-condition comparisons, neuronal diversity and local distance-dependent V1 connectivity make separable, additive contributions that break rigid sequential pipelines and raise spike-order divergence to levels matching mouse V1 recordings, while silencing 100 high-information early-informer neurons flips low-dimensional decision bifurcations.
diagram_caption: Local connectivity and cellular diversity shape sparse spike-order sequences that guide visual decisions.

title: Bridging Scales: Spectral Theory Reveals How Local Connectivity Rules Sculpt Global Neural Dynamics in Spatially Extended Networks
summary: Analytical spatial spectral theory maps microscopic excitatory-inhibitory connectivity footprints to bulk and outlier eigenvalue signatures that predict macroscopic waves, bumps, oscillations, and chaos.
question: How do local distance-dependent excitatory and inhibitory wiring rules determine global spatiotemporal brain dynamics?
motivation: Across behavioral and arousal states, cortical populations shift among asynchronous activity, global oscillations, localized working-memory bumps, and traveling waves. Because brute-force simulations cannot systematically map high-dimensional anatomical parameter spaces, a closed-form mathematical bridge is needed between microscopic synaptic projection rules and macroscopic dynamical regimes.
idea: For two-dimensional spatially extended excitatory-inhibitory networks with Gaussian distance-decaying connection probabilities and cell-type coupling strengths, we derive an analytical spectral decomposition of the effective connectivity Jacobian. Synaptic variance determines a circular bulk eigenvalue disk governing chaotic instability, whereas mean spatial excitation-inhibition profiles generate discrete Fourier outlier eigenvalues whose real, imaginary, and wavenumber coordinates select coherent spatial and temporal modes.
finding_title: Closed-Form Phase Diagrams Across Scales
finding: The eigenvalue spectrum analytically predicts transitions across six macroscopic regimes (quiescent, synchronous, homogeneous oscillatory, stationary bump, traveling wave, and high-dimensional asynchronous chaos) and extends via linear-response approximations to conductance-based spiking networks. Comparing predicted phase boundaries with mesoscale cortical recordings across anesthetized and awake states provides preliminary evidence and a principled starting point for inferring microscopic effective connectivity shifts from macroscopic activity.
diagram_caption: Local spatial connectivity parameters determine spectral signatures that govern macroscopic neural dynamics.

title: SpikeGrasp: A Benchmark for 6-DoF Grasp Pose Detection from Stereo Spike Streams
summary: SpikeGrasp predicts 6-DoF robotic grasp poses directly from binocular spike streams via adaptive recurrent spiking refinement, bypassing explicit 3D point-cloud reconstruction.
question: Can embodied robotic systems infer 6-DoF grasp poses directly from stereo spike streams without intermediate point clouds?
motivation: Standard robotic grasping pipelines reconstruct 3D point clouds from RGB-D cameras before planning contacts, a two-stage process vulnerable to motion blur, specular or textureless surfaces, and extreme lighting. Biological dorsal visuomotor pathways instead transform continuous binocular retinal spike streams directly into motor actions through recurrent dynamical integration.
idea: SpikeGrasp processes raw binocular \(400 \times 250\) spike streams through multiscale stereo feature extractors and cross-view correlation matching, feeding an Iterative Spiking Refinement Module composed of adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire recurrent units directly into an end-to-end 6-DoF grasp detection head. Persistent membrane-potential states continuously integrate asynchronous disparity and contour cues across time without frame or depth-map reconstruction.
finding_title: Data-Efficient Grasping Under Extreme Lighting
finding: Evaluated on the SpikeGrasp-1B synthetic benchmark (190 scenes, 88 objects, over 1 billion grasp annotations) and 240 physical Franka Emika Panda robot trials, SpikeGrasp outperforms two-stage depth-plus-point-cloud pipelines including AnyGrasp, GraspGen, and GSNet. It achieves \(1.4\times\) to \(2.2\times\) higher synthetic precision when trained on 10% data and reaches 85.0% overall real-world grasp success, maintaining 83.3% success under high-dynamic-range lighting where frame baselines drop to 36.7%.
diagram_caption: Stereo spike streams feed directly into a recurrent spiking network to predict grasp poses.
version_note: The earlier arXiv preprint was withdrawn. The figure is from a different manuscript supplied by the author.

title: SPKLIP: Aligning Spike Video Streams with Natural Language
summary: SPKLIP aligns continuous high-speed spike camera streams with natural language via hierarchical multiscale temporal modeling and contrastive learning, supporting sample- and energy-efficient transfer.
question: How can sparse, microsecond-resolved binary spike video streams be aligned directly with natural language semantics?
motivation: Vision-language models such as CLIP rely on dense RGB encoders that mismatch the binary, ultra-high-frame-rate output of neuromorphic spike cameras, while reconstructing intensity frames from spikes introduces motion blur and heavy preprocessing overhead. Unlocking multimodal understanding for high-speed neuromorphic vision requires native encoders that extract semantics directly from multi-timescale spike dynamics.
idea: SPKLIP pairs a pretrained text encoder with a three-stage Hierarchical Spike-stream Feature Extractor combining local convolutions and shifted-window Transformers, coupled to a Multi-scale Temporal Interaction Module that attends across \(1\times\), \(2\times\), and \(4\times\) temporal strides to fuse rapid motion transients with coarse action context. A Full-Spiking Visual Encoder variant replaces floating-point activations with binary leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics for neuromorphic efficiency.
finding_title: High-Speed Action Alignment and Few-Shot Transfer
finding: Trained from scratch via symmetric contrastive learning, SPKLIP achieves 91.15% Top-1 accuracy on HMDB51-S and 86.43% on UCF101-S, outperforming prior spike recognition and reconstructed-frame CLIP baselines. On newly recorded real-world RealSpike camera streams, few-shot adaptation rises from 62.37% (2-shot) to 80.81% (4-shot), 87.88% (6-shot), and 90.41% (8-shot) Top-1 accuracy. On UCF101-S at \(T = 2\), replacing floating-point visual blocks with spiking variants cuts estimated encoding energy by 75.8% from 1.469 J in Raw-SPKLIP (86.43% Top-1) to 0.356 J, retaining 71.11% Top-1 accuracy in SPKLIP-1 (spiking CNN only) and 65.24% in SPKLIP-2 (spiking CNN and Transformer).
diagram_caption: Hierarchical temporal features extracted from spike streams align with text in a shared space.

title: Unveiling and Steering Connectome Organization with Interpretable Latent Variables
summary: An explainable graph-attention generative model extracts low-dimensional latent variables from Drosophila FlyWire visual subgraphs to decode motif organization and steer bio-plausible circuit synthesis.
question: Can interpretable latent variables uncover the organizational rules of biological connectomes and steer synthetic circuit design?
motivation: Whole-brain connectomes such as Drosophila FlyWire expose intricate synaptic wiring across cell and neurotransmitter types, yet evolved circuits develop from compact genetic bottlenecks rather than arbitrary edge lists. Identifying interpretable low-dimensional coordinates that govern recurrent motifs is critical for turning raw connectome maps into controllable architectural priors.
idea: We sample 500 cylindrical subgraphs (81 to 100 neurons annotated with four neurotransmitter classes) along the Drosophila visual pathway and train a multi-head Graph Attention Variational Autoencoder using balanced \(1 + 2n\) positive-to-negative edge sampling for sparse connectivity. A surrogate topological predictor paired with Shapley additive explanations maps individual latent axes onto structural properties, enabling closed-loop latent optimization via dynamic programming and CMA-ES.
finding_title: Disentangled Motif Axes and Targeted Synthesis
finding: The learned latent code reconstructs sparse biological subgraphs with substantially lower structural discrepancy than classical random-graph models (clustering MMD 0.056 versus 0.215 to 0.562) while isolating specific axes associated with reciprocity, clustering, hub structure, and degree dispersion. Steering those interpretable coordinates synthesizes bio-plausible circuits matching prescribed topological targets, reaching 0.919 AUC when guided by complete target-graph information and 0.852 AUC when guided solely by target statistical information.
diagram_caption: Connectome subgraphs map to interpretable latent axes that steer synthetic circuit topology.

title: Neural heterogeneity enhances reliable neural information processing: Local sensitivity and globally input-slaved transient dynamics
summary: Dissociated neuronal and synaptic heterogeneities break autonomous cortical waves to create locally sensitive, globally input-slaved transient trajectories for reliable, noise-robust computation.
question: How does biophysical heterogeneity enable noisy cortical circuits to encode external signals reliably across trials?
motivation: Cortical neurons exhibit pronounced diversity in membrane timescales, thresholds, and connectivity alongside substantial trial-to-trial spike variability. How recurrent circuits reconcile single-neuron irregularity with reproducible population coding, and why biological diversity consistently improves temporal computation over homogeneous networks, lacked a unified dynamical explanation.
idea: In 50,000-neuron spatially extended excitatory-inhibitory spiking networks, we introduce empirical lognormal diversity in dissociated membrane leakage (\(\tau_L\)) and response-gain (\(\tau_{\Gamma}\)) timescales, as well as spike-threshold, in-degree, and spatial input-weight heterogeneities. Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition and perturbation analyses, we track how diversity transforms autonomous Turing-Hopf traveling waves and 1D asynchronous states under periodic and chaotic driving.
finding_title: Expanded Representation Space and Reservoir Reliability
finding: Dissociated heterogeneity disrupts rigid intrinsic wave coherence, inducing firing-rate diversity and heightened local responsiveness that excite global input-specific nonlinear wave modes. The resulting high-dimensional, input-slaved transient trajectories remain reproducible across strong noise perturbations despite variable individual spikes, markedly elevating signal-to-noise ratio and lowering reconstruction error on nonlinear harmonic generation and multiscale chaotic Mackey-Glass and Lorenz reservoir tasks.
diagram_caption: Biological heterogeneity disrupts autonomous waves so network transients reliably track external inputs.

title: Evolutionary learning in neural networks by heterosynaptic plasticity
summary: Combining interneuron-gated dendritic routing with dopamine-guided heterosynaptic plasticity enables gradient-free evolutionary learning across biophysical spiking and deep binary-weight networks.
question: How can cortical circuits optimize multi-layer and recurrent biophysical networks using strictly forward, non-backpropagating mechanisms?
motivation: Error backpropagation requires symmetric feedback weight transport and smooth derivatives that clash with physical synapses and strongly nonlinear spiking biophysics, whereas purely local Hebbian updates struggle to coordinate multi-layer credit assignment. Cortical circuits possess parallel dendritic pathways, neuromodulators, and non-local heterosynaptic signals that could support an alternative optimization principle.
idea_title: Dendritic Pathway Selection and Heterosynaptic Copy
idea: We map evolutionary optimization onto experimentally grounded circuit substrates: alternating dendritic pathways gated by interneuron and thalamocortical control act as candidate routing agents; dopamine evaluates pathway fitness; nitric-oxide and astrocyte-mediated heterosynaptic plasticity copies high-performing weights across neighboring synapses; synchronous group mutations (\(<5\%\) flips per epoch) and dopamine meta-plasticity preserve elite solutions during dual-timescale offline replay.
finding_title: Prefrontal Line Attractors and Gradient-Free Competence
finding: Trained purely through forward passes, recurrent networks self-organize monkey-like prefrontal psychometric curves, evidence-proportional line attractors, and context-orthogonal selection vectors in context-dependent decision-making. The same binary-weight evolutionary rule trains recurrent spiking networks to generate target temporal trajectories, matches continuous-weight backpropagation on multi-layer MNIST where layerwise Hebbian learning degrades, and achieves Atari scores competitive with continuous-weight DQN and A3C across 13 games.
diagram_caption: Evolutionary pathway selection and dopamine-driven heterosynaptic plasticity jointly optimize biophysical networks.

title: Data-based large-scale models provide a window into the organization of cortical computations
summary: Reverse-engineering a task-trained 51,978-neuron mouse V1 model with layer-5 projection readouts uncovers soft rank-order coding, nested trajectory bifurcations, and strong functional segregation.
question: How do laminar anatomy and diverse neuron biophysics organize internal computations inside cortical microcircuits?
motivation: Conventional recurrent neural network models of cortex extract decisions through dense global linear readouts over all units, allowing readout weights to solve tasks even without internal circuit computation. Uncovering how biological microcircuits actually organize sensory memory and decisions requires anatomically realistic models constrained to communicate through sparse projection neurons.
idea: We train a data-based 51,978-neuron mouse V1 microcircuit comprising 111 Allen GLIF3 neuron variants across five cortical layers on natural-image change detection and sequential evidence accumulation, reporting decisions solely through layer-5 pyramidal projection neurons. We compare single-trial dynamics against Neuropixels recordings from 20 mice, five structural ablations, and matched recurrent artificial, convolutional, and generic spiking networks.
finding_title: Nested Bifurcations Driven by Early-Informer Cells
finding: Unlike artificial and generic spiking controls, the trained V1 circuit reproduces experimental soft rank-order coding (cross-condition Kendall's \(\tau = 0.004\), matching 0.003 in 20 mice versus 0.273 in RANN/RCNN) and high functional segregation (0.21 versus 0.02), both dependent on laminar wiring and cell-type diversity. Slow GLIF3 after-spike currents retain prior-stimulus memory in layer-2/3 and layer-4 early-informer neurons; silencing just 100 of them flips the 50 to 100 ms state-space decision bifurcation and reverses projection-neuron output.
diagram_caption: Anatomically constrained microcircuit models trained on tasks reveal sparse cortical computing mechanisms.

title: A data-based large-scale model for primary visual cortex enables brain-like robust and versatile visual processing
summary: A data-constrained 51,978-neuron model of mouse primary visual cortex solves five diverse spatial and temporal visual tasks with one weight matrix while exhibiting sparse coding and strong out-of-distribution noise robustness.
question: Can an anatomically and physiologically realistic primary visual cortex model achieve versatile, noise-resilient visual processing?
motivation: Convolutional neural networks excel on narrow static benchmarks yet differ fundamentally from mammalian visual cortex: they use uniform non-spiking units, narrow local fan-in, and feedforward hierarchies that remain brittle to unseen noise distributions and unable to integrate temporally dispersed cues within a single shared sensory circuit.
idea_title: Multi-Task Training of Data-Constrained Area V1
idea: Integrating Allen Institute anatomical and electrophysiological data, we train a 3D laminar column of 51,978 spiking GLIF3 neurons spanning 111 cell variants in 17 excitatory and inhibitory classes, driven by 17,400 LGN spatiotemporal filters under empirical quick and slow cortical noise (\(\text{Fano factor} = 1.46\)) and read out via local 30-neuron layer-5 pyramidal pools across five spatial and working-memory visual tasks.
finding_title: Multi-Task Versatility and Orthogonal Noise Coding
finding: With one shared synaptic weight matrix, the V1 model reaches 94.28% mean accuracy across 0.1-degree orientation discrimination, MNIST classification, grating and natural-image change detection, and sequential evidence accumulation at \(\sim 4\,\mathrm{Hz}\) sparse firing and near-critical branching dynamics. Laminar structure and 111-type neuron diversity induce a biological power-law PCA eigenspectrum and align signal dimensions nearly orthogonal to dominant correlated noise modes, conferring zero-shot out-of-distribution robustness to unseen pixel and internal noise.
diagram_caption: Anatomically grounded V1 circuitry generates sparse neural codes that support noise-robust visual tasks.

title: A spatiotemporal mechanism of visual attention: Superdiffusive motion and theta oscillations of neural population activity patterns
summary: Operating near a critical wave-asynchrony transition with spike-frequency adaptation, cortical circuits generate an oscillatory attention spotlight that samples visual scenes via superdiffusive Levy jumps.
question: What circuit architecture and dynamical regime produce rhythmic fluctuations and efficient spatial sampling in visual attention?
motivation: Electrophysiological and behavioral studies show that visual attention is neither static nor deterministically ordered: attentional sampling fluctuates at theta (\(\sim 4\,\mathrm{Hz}\)) rhythms coupled to gamma bursts atop arrhythmic \(1/f\) background activity, while shifting rapidly across distant targets. Classical winner-take-all models generate rigid, distance-dependent sequences that miss this dynamical richness.
idea: We model two-dimensional spatially extended excitatory-inhibitory spiking circuits (corroborated by bifurcation analysis of adaptive firing-rate sheets) incorporating distance-dependent coupling at physiological inhibition-to-excitation balance (\(\zeta_c = 3.31\)) and excitatory slow potassium spike-frequency adaptation. We analyze the emergent motion of localized population spotlights across dual-target paradigms and 1,003 natural scenes alongside a fractional momentum stochastic differential equation.
finding_title: Theta-Gamma Coupling and Superdiffusive Exploration
finding: Only near the critical transition between asynchronous firing and propagating waves does the circuit intrinsically generate variable \(\sim 4\,\mathrm{Hz}\) theta oscillations riding on \(1/f\) activity (exponent 1.2), theta-phase-locked gamma bursts (\(>60\,\mathrm{Hz}\)), and heavy-tailed Levy displacements (\(\alpha = 1.27\)). Across MIT1003 natural scenes, the spotlight outperforms winner-take-all models in matching human attention maps and trial-by-trial scanpath variability, algorithmically uniting Levy jumps with oscillatory momentum to balance local exploitation and global exploration.
diagram_caption: Transition-regime circuit dynamics drive an oscillatory spotlight that samples visual scenes superdiffusively.

title: Anomalous diffusion dynamics of learning in deep neural networks
summary: Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent interacts with fractal-like deep network loss landscapes to drive early superdiffusive weight jumps across sharp barriers toward wide, generalizable minima.
question: How do loss-landscape geometry and mini-batch gradient dynamics govern escape from sharp local minima in deep networks?
motivation: Classical optimization theories often approximate stochastic gradient descent as standard Brownian motion in a continuous Langevin potential. Yet Brownian diffusion with small isotropic steps becomes exponentially trapped in rugged high-dimensional landscapes, leaving unexplained how overparameterized deep networks rapidly escape sharp, poorly generalizing basins.
idea: Using statistical-physics diagnostics of rough landscapes, we quantify mean-squared weight displacements, step-size statistics, trajectory fractal and transverse-distance geometry, mean squared loss scaling, two-dimensional landscape projections with box counting, and leading Hessian eigenvalues across residual networks (ResNet-14, 20, 56, and 110) and skip-free VGG-like architectures trained on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under varying batch sizes and learning rates.
finding_title: Fractal Geometry Induces Two-Stage Anomalous Diffusion
finding: Rather than following Brownian motion, SGD weight updates interact with self-similar, fractal-like loss surfaces (mean squared loss scaling exponent \(2H = 1.8\), corresponding to Hurst exponent \(H\) near 0.9) to generate non-Gaussian, directionally correlated steps, a mechanism corroborated in a simplified SGD model driven by Gaussian noise on a synthetic two-dimensional fractal landscape. Learning unfolds in two dynamical regimes: early superdiffusion (diffusion exponent \(>1\)) that crosses sharp barriers, followed by late subdiffusion (exponent \(<1\)) that settles inside wide minima characterized by smaller top-20 Hessian eigenvalues and stronger test generalization.
diagram_caption: Fractal loss geometry induces superdiffusive gradient steps that escape sharp traps toward wide minima.

title: ViR:the Vision Reservoir
summary: Vision Reservoir replaces trainable Transformer self-attention blocks with fixed small-world recurrent reservoirs, achieving parameter- and memory-efficient image classification without pretraining.
question: Can structured fixed recurrent reservoirs substitute for trainable self-attention in data-constrained visual recognition from scratch?
motivation: Vision Transformers rely on quadratic multi-head self-attention layers whose weak spatial inductive bias demands massive pretraining datasets, high parameter counts, and heavy activation memory, causing severe overfitting when trained from scratch on modest visual benchmarks.
idea: Splitting images into patch token sequences, Vision Reservoir (including single-layer ViR, hierarchical Series-ViR, and multi-branch Parallel-ViR) replaces multi-head self-attention with fixed recurrent modules built with a nearly fully connected topology, constructed by randomly zeroing symmetric element pairs, randomly assigning positive and negative synaptic signs under edge-of-stability spectral scaling, and projecting tokens through sparse random input matrices (yielding small-worldness 1.02) while training only lightweight embeddings and readout layers.
finding_title: Pretraining-Free Accuracy at Fraction of Cost
finding: Dynamical analysis links peak classification accuracy to near-unit spectral radii, near-zero largest Lyapunov exponents, and high short-term memory capacity that mix patch sequences without gradient backpropagation through attention maps. Trained from scratch without external pretraining on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 (and evaluated under CIFAR-10-C corruptions), Parallel-ViR surpasses depth-matched Vision Transformers while requiring 5% to 15% of the parameters and 20% to 40% of the memory footprint.
diagram_caption: Image token sequences project through a fixed recurrent reservoir for lightweight visual classification.

title: Computing by modulating spontaneous cortical activity patterns as a mechanism of active visual processing
summary: Near criticality, sensory inputs compute by reshaping and trapping ongoing spontaneous cortical waves rather than driving spikes from silence, accelerating active perception and explaining perceptual bubbles.
question: How do ongoing spontaneous cortical waves actively contribute to rapid sensory coding and visual perception?
motivation: Even without external input, sensory cortex consumes substantial metabolic energy generating coherent, propagating waves whose spatial correlations mirror evoked responses and influence trial-by-trial spike latency. Treating this ongoing activity as background noise to be averaged away leaves its computational role in active perception unresolved.
idea: In a 62,500-neuron V1-scale conductance-based spiking circuit with distance-dependent excitation and inhibition, we analyze spontaneous pattern propagation across dynamical phase transitions and stimulate the circuit with natural scenes and Difference-of-Gaussians face images, complemented by an analytical stochastic walker model in a logarithmic stimulus potential.
finding_title: Critical Wave Trapping and Perceptual Bubbles
finding: At the critical transition between asynchronous and coherent wave states, symmetry breaking generates scale-free propagating patterns (size exponent 1.59, duration exponent 2.25) that reproduce patchy resting-state correlation fractures. External stimuli reshape and trap these ongoing patterns to generate 80.05% of evoked spikes, shortening stimulus decoding latency from 216.4 ms to 165.9 ms, explaining intracellular pre-stimulus voltage-to-latency correlations and power-law reaction times, and matching human face-recognition perceptual bubbles (mean correlation 0.67).
diagram_caption: External stimuli reshape ongoing spontaneous cortical waves to accelerate active visual perception.
